anjali (support): Customer EchoPay reporting intermittent 504/5xx + timeouts since 2026-03-17 09:10 UTC. p95 latency spikes to 12s, some requests return 504. Ticket INC-12345. Attaching trace IDs. Can SRE/Runtime triage?

 dino-bot: alert: ingress.pool.hosted-us-west-2-1 queue_depth=198/200 (98%), continuous_batcher.backlog=820, kv_cache_miss_rate=27% :warning:

 marie (oncall): I'm on it. Which model & seq len? QPS pattern? Any auth/billing spikes?

 anjali (support): Customer uses text-generate /v1/generate model=redwood-2b, avg_seq=1024, 95th_seq=2048, sustained concurrent RPS ~110-130 for last 30m. No billing auth errors reported.

 chris (eng-runtime): seeing same in traces. sample logs:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:01Z] pool=hosted-us-west-2-1 batcher.backlog=820 queue_depth=198 dequeue_latency_ms=1187 early_rejects=0 gateway.rsp.5xx=12
```
queue depth cap is 200; requests sit in queue waiting for batcher to schedule => long tail. Once request exceeds gateway deadline we return 504.

 sam (sre): root cause looks like continuous-batcher can't keep up with token emission due to long seqs & high qps; KV cache misses worsen it. We also saw increased context-length variance from EchoPay => larger batches take longer.

 leah (product): Customer is on hosted. Can't change their reserved capacity. Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) ask client to cap concurrency; 2) route them to a smaller model for peak hours; 3) enable temporary burst capacity for the pool; 4) enable prefix/KV caching on their tenant.

 chris (eng-runtime): immediate patch we can do now: enable tenant-level early_rejects and tenant qps throttle for EchoPay. Example config to apply:
```
{ "tenant": "echopay", "qps_limit": 60, "early_reject": true }
```
This will fail fast instead of queueing to 200.

 marie (oncall): repro steps for local testing:
1) run locust/hey with 140 rps targeting /v1/generate
2) payload len ~1024, model redwood-2b
3) monitor batcher.backlog and pool queue_depth
Example curl loop (nonblocking):
```
for i in {1..500}; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @payload.json & done
```

 anjali (support): I'll pass recommended mitigations to EchoPay (qps cap + temporary smaller model). Requested escalation to Sales for burst capacity offer.

 dino-bot: monitor: queue_depth dropped to 80/200 after tenant qps=60 applied. p95 latency back to 450ms. :white_check_mark:

 anjali (support): Customer accepts workaround for now. Will track if they need dedicated capacity. Closing interim support loop. Thanks all.
